added_items.title: AI boom or doom: what will superintelligence feel like and when will we get there?
summary_points: AGI Timeline & Market Inflection: Deutsche Bank identifies 2030 as critical for AGI (self-improving AI exceeding human cognition), with industry signals (OpenAI 2026, Google level 5) driving market disruption; portfolio positioning must address both boom (AGI growth) and doom (rogue AI, energy costs).

Infrastructure Capital Flow: Hyperscalers (Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle) plan $800B+ in 2023 data center spend, scaling to $1T+/year through 2030—critical for AGI but constrained by grid delays (years-long lead times) and geopolitical hurdles.

Data Scarcity Bottleneck: Public human text tokens (300T) will deplete by 2026–2032, forcing reliance on synthetic data; trust in "checker" inputs becomes a critical risk as LLM training datasets approach saturation (median 2028 full stock use).

Sectoral Disruption Asymmetry: Post-ChatGPT (Nov 2022), semiconductors/semi-equipment surged 7x vs software +80%, invalidating traditional diversification; "adopters" (regulated sectors, proprietary data) outperform "casualties" with no overlap.

Infrastructure Cost Ceiling: AGI training requires 10³⁰ FLOPs (vs current 10²²), needing 6GW power (50% more than US nuclear plants) and $300B–$500B compute cost; frontier chips demand 26GW power ($900B today), creating capital/energy constraints.

added_items.title: GS DeGrasse Desk Bank Fins EPS Preview 7 Oct 2026
summary_points: Capital Markets/NII Dynamics: Rising rates pressure NII amid fixed-rate asset repricing delays and deposit cost competition, creating near-term earnings headwinds despite strong 2Q26 IB outlook.

AI/credit deployment trajectory: Strategic pivot on AI (competition vs. margin expansion) and credit deployment pace into 2027 are critical for sector growth, with financial institutions facing strategic trade-offs.
US Consumer Finance Underperformance: -9.9% return since last EPS season (vs. sector -3.9%), driven by macro/oil tail risks and constrained multiples, signaling significant sector-specific risk.

added_items.title: Americas Capital Markets Round tripped
summary_points: Rates-Driven Sector Rotation: Exchanges outperformed (+16.6% QTD) due to volume surges in Energy/Rates (e.g., ICE energy vol +18% y/y), while Alternatives underperformed (-3.2% QTD) amid rates-driven reversal and EPS risks.
EPS Revisions Dominance: YTD 2027 EPS revisions explain 63% of price performance variance (R²=0.63), confirming EPS as the primary driver for stock returns across sectors.

Valuation Discrepancy: Alternatives (e.g., APO, ARES) trade at 15%-20% discounts to 5-year P/E averages (17X NTM vs. 24X historical), while Traditional Asset Managers (e.g., AMG, APAM) trade at premiums.

Key Upside Catalysts: Alternative Asset Managers (e.g., STEP, TPG) show 100% and 21%+ 2025-28E FRE/share CAGR, with STEP at 100% upside; Exchanges (TW, ICE) benefit from AI-driven Energy volumes and Rates demand.

added_items.title: JPM Asia Thematic Strategy (must read)
summary_points: AI Hardware Supply-Demand Tightness: Hardware layer (Taiwan/Korea/China) faces persistent supply-demand imbalance through 2028, enabling $1T+ net income for AI ecosystem by 2028 and driving 70% of 2027 earnings growth in Asia.
Hyperscaler FCF Closure Timeline: Hyperscaler AI FCF hole closes by 2028, with 30%+ ROI on datacenters (5-year depreciation) and minimal interest rate sensitivity, critical for cash flow dynamics.
AI Model Layer Monetization: $300bn+ ARR by end-2026 (3x 2025), driven by token volume (not pricing), enterprise adoption, and fading token subsidies, signaling structural revenue growth.
Asia Hardware Dominance: Taiwan/Korea exceed 50% of Asia AI hardware exposure (vs.
US software/hardware mix), with TSMC/Samsung/Hynix dominating top holdings and concentration risks in ecosystem.
